subject: Clarifying custody and proof-of-delete for VPC storage (narrow scoping)
messages:
From: Lia Zhang <lia.zhang@healthbridge.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T09:12:00-07:00
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com
Subject: Narrow-scope questions on VPC storage custody + deletion proof

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move forward with a Private/VPC deployment, our security and legal teams need a tight, auditable description of how customer-controlled storage works and what evidence Redwood can provide when we ask for deletion or residency assurances.

High-level questions (we'd like short, actionable answers):
- What artifacts can Redwood provide to prove a tenant's data was removed from active storage and backups (evidence-of-delete)?
- Do you offer an attestation or signed certificate for a one-time wipe, and what is the expected timeline?
- How do you handle snapshots, object-store replication, and cross-region caching for VPC-deployed stores?
- If we bring our own KMS keys (BYOK), can Redwood perform a physical key rotation or destruction on our behalf to force unrecoverability?
- Any constraints for EU residency (data never leaving eu-west-1) and proof we can show auditors?

Appreciate short bullets we can pass to InfoSec. If it's easier, we can do a 30-minute call.

Regards,
Lia Zhang
Head of Security, HealthBridge

P.S. attaching our standard data-handling questionnaire as a reference (we will share it in a separate email).

From: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-07-10T10:05:00-07:00
To: Lia Zhang <lia.zhang@healthbridge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Subject: Re: Narrow-scope questions on VPC storage custody + deletion proof

Lia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front; details below and an attached draft SOW/term sheet for the Private deployment.

- Evidence-of-delete: we can provide immutable audit logs (object-level delete events), storage tombstone records, and a signed deletion attestation (PDF) that references object IDs and timestamps. For snapshot-level data, we can provide snapshot manifests and checksums showing deletion of snapshot entries.
- Attestation: yes — we routinely produce a signed attestation for tenant wipe operations. Typical turnaround: 3 business days after the wipe completes and logs are consolidated. If you need an independent auditor attestation, we can coordinate (timeline varies).
- Snapshots/replication: for Private/VPC you can choose the storage policy. If configured for single-region/eu-west-1 only, we will disable cross-region replication and periodic caching to other regions. Snapshots are incremental; when a snapshot references deleted objects we mark the manifest and can purge underlying blocks during the wipe flow.
- BYOK: you retain key control. We can execute a key-rotation workflow, and if you request key destruction we will perform the steps in our procedure (we will not destroy customer keys within your KMS; instead we remove any Redwood-held wrapped keys and, if requested, publish a destruction attestation). Note: we cannot operate your external HSM directly — you must perform the final key deletion in your KMS.
- EU residency: we support tenancy pinned to eu-west-1, disable cross-region replication and backups to other regions, and provide region-scoped audit logs.

Next steps I propose:
1) We attach SOW_TermSheet_v2.pdf with the custody language included — please review.
2) Marissa (Ops) will add the technical purge timeline and evidence artifacts we can produce.
3) Ben (sales) will outline the licensing path for Private deployment/BYOK.

Would you like a brief call tomorrow to walk the checklist?

— Soojin
So, Soojin Lee
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM Lia Zhang <lia.zhang@healthbridge.com> wrote:
> High-level questions (we'd like short, actionable answers):
> - What artifacts can Redwood provide to prove a tenant's data was removed from active storage and backups (evidence-of-delete)?
> - Do you offer an attestation or signed certificate for a one-time wipe, and what is the expected timeline?

Adding technical detail here so you have an operational checklist for InfoSec: 

1) Delete artifacts we can provide (operational):
   - Object-store delete events (immutable audit log entries with object ID, bucket/path, timestamp, and actor ID).
   - Snapshot manifests: lists of objects present at each snapshot with SHA256 checksums and manifest IDs. We can show a manifest before and after purge to demonstrate removal.
   - Block/extent reclamation records: when we scrub underlying blocks for storage backends that support block-level purge. Not all backends expose this; if you require it we should list it in the SOW.

2) Timeline expectations (private, single-region):
   - Immediate object delete: deletion event written synchronously.
   - Snapshot purge window: snapshots referencing deleted objects are marked; actual block reclamation depends on backend GC cycles — typical window 48–168 hours (2–7 days) for most configurations.
   - Complete scrub and attestation generation: target 3 business days after GC completes and logs are verified. If cross-account replication was disabled at teardown start, GC windows shorten.

3) BYOK specifics:
   - If HealthBridge provides KMS keys in your cloud provider, you manage final key destruction. Redwood purges any locally cached wrapped material and will produce an attestation stating that no wrapped copies remain in Redwood systems.
   - If you require Redwood to execute a KMS-based key rotation (e.g., schedule a key disable as part of the teardown), include API credentials and explicit approval in the SOW and an auditable operation runbook.

4) Evidence formats: signed PDF attestation (includes manifest IDs, delete timestamps, and auditor statement), CSV export of audit log rows, and an S3/secure share of the snapshot manifests (checksummed).

5) Limits/edge cases:
   - Third-party backup integrations (if you snapshot to a third-party backup product) require us to coordinate with that vendor — list that vendor in the SOW.
   - Cold backups stored off-cluster (if enabled) may have different purge policies; we recommend disabling these for EU-pinned workloads unless explicitly required.

I'm happy to draft the checklist as a short 1-page appendix to the SOW (technical purge checklist + evidence pack).

Lia — attaching the requested artifacts and next steps.

Attachments included: SOW_TermSheet_v2.pdf (updated residency paragraphs + appendix placeholder), custody_flow_v1.png (diagram used by Ops for the purge workflow), and a 1-page Evidence-of-Delete checklist (embedded in SOW appendix).

Quick summary of the commitments added to the SOW appendix:
- Residency: tenant storage and all audit logs are pinned to eu-west-1; cross-region replication disabled.
- Audit log retention default: 90 days (configurable). We listed 90 days as the default for review; happy to negotiate a longer retention term if required.
- Wipe timeline: final block reclamation targeted within 7 days (typical), attestation issued within 3 business days after reclaim completes.
- Evidence pack: signed attestation PDF, CSV audit export, and snapshot manifests (checksums).
- BYOK: Redwood purges all locally-held wrapped key material and will provide a wrapped-key-purge attestation; final KMS deletion remains in customer control.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached SOW_TermSheet_v2.pdf and call out any redlines by reply or in the DocuSign flow. DocuSign link: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/ABC123456789
2) Marissa will finalize the 1-page checklist as an appendix once HealthBridge confirms the 90-day log retention default or proposes an alternative.
3) Ben will issue the commercial addendum reflecting the Private deployment commit.

Would you like a short call tomorrow at 10:00 AM CET to walk legal through the wording? If yes I will send an invite.

— Soojin
